cases.title: Actual acceptance after waiting anchors the full period
Crossing the displayed end date requires refreshed terms
cases.unsafe: silently accept a different end date

cases.title: Adding a local calendar day can produce 23 or 25 elapsed hours
A preview's cached UTC offset can misstate the actual endpoint by an hour
Date-only truncation loses part of the promised elapsed period
Absent, coerced or unsupported periods cannot manufacture a valid window
cases.unsafe: parse, truncate, default or accept any positive-looking value

cases.title: A range-valid period still needs checked timestamp representation
cases.unsafe: clamp, wrap, truncate or store an unrepresentable endpoint

cases.title: A changed period fences unaccepted review and never rewrites an accepted cycle
cases.unsafe: apply latest period to pending command or recompute every current deadline

cases.title: Period value returning to its old value does not revive the old review
Stable absent-policy review cannot be upgraded by first configure and enable
cases.unsafe: saving a period enables continuation or fills old request defaults

cases.title: Lost-response or late-delivery recovery preserves the original endpoint even Off and later expired
cases.unsafe: anchor a new deadline at retry, webhook delivery or current period

cases.title: Ordinary activity does not run a renewed-window clock or restore personal data
The exact stored endpoint is exclusive without waiting for a sweep or end of local day
cases.unsafe: active through equality, local midnight or next sweep

cases.title: The explanatory endpoint is not caller-supplied date-setting authority
cases.unsafe: submit the displayed or edited endpoint as the new source deadline

cases.title: Time-only source expiry cannot upgrade an already rejected intent
cases.unsafe: forget terminal no-effect, then retry when time makes source eligible

cases.title: Explicit toy owner-range endpoints produce exact finite elapsed periods
No-op save and ordinary seconds of waiting need no extra confirmation
Fresh deliberate review can accept changed displayed terms while the old intent stays rejected
Ordinary staff and missionary continuation use the same period without coupling staff to missionary On
A later deliberate cycle captures new policy while the old cycle stays immutable
Ordinary offset advance within the same displayed zone/date accepts with coherent actual rendering

decision: D36 uses the organization's configured finite renewed period, without a per-continuation date override
limitations: Only this new synthetic standard-library model runs; no older model/probe/verifier, app, SQL/RLS, database, provider, network or private data is exercised.
Current action/source/result authority are opaque qualified inputs inherited from D35, not retested P9/P12 producers or a full authorization model.
Ordered acceptance assumes authoritative clock and atomic current facts. Actual lock waits, transaction-start clocks, clock skew/rollback, replicas, concurrency and crash durability are not proved.

The toy integer range 1..400 is not a product limit/default. Actual supported bounds, numeric transport types, settings authority and representable production timestamp domain remain owner qualification work.
Python aware datetime has microsecond precision and no leap-second representation; these examples do not prove production precision, arithmetic, serialization or database timestamp limits.

America/New_York uses the execution environment's IANA zoneinfo data for explicit 2026 examples; no production tzdb version, locale format, timezone preference product or UI witness authenticity is qualified.

Reviewed zone/date are explanatory witness fixtures, never caller authority to write a date. An ordinary offset advance within the same zone/date is accepted and the actual endpoint is rendered with its own offset. Actual UI/accessibility, context binding and late responses are untested.

outcomes is narrow semantic owner evidence, not a table/generic command journal. Terminal evidence persists for this finite run; lawful retirement must retain a non-replay fence and is not implemented here.
Read-only activity examples compare stored facts with an unsafe reset formula; they do not run actual view/edit/login hooks, tasks, consent, grant expiry, retention or external integrations.
Finite examples are not exhaustive scheduling, formal verification, a deployed grant, activation qualification or release readiness.
status: proposed elapsed-day and temporal owner contract illustration; not ratification or runtime proof
unit: One elapsed day is exactly 86400 seconds; E is computed from actual authoritative acceptance A after waits in UTC.
